How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

Below is a quick‑start guide that walks you through the exact steps you’ll take inside the **Cisco Nexus Dashboard** UI to generate a ready‑to‑copy RESTful request for the *“get information of device connector versions”* API (the one you mentioned – version 6.3.1). I’ve also added a short “copy‑and‑paste” example that you can drop straight into your terminal or Postman once you’ve filled in the placeholders. --- ## 1️⃣ Log In & Open the API Explorer | Step | What to do | Screenshot hint | |------|------------|------------------| | 1 | Open your browser and navigate to the Nexus Dashboard URL (e.g. `https://nexus-dashboard.example.com`). | ![Login screen](https://example.com/login.png) | | 2 | Enter your credentials (or use SSO) and hit **Log In**. | ![Dashboard home](https://example.com/home.png) | | 3 | From the left‑hand navigation pane, click **Developer** → **API Explorer**. | ![API Explorer link](https://example.com/api-explorer-link.png) | > **Tip:** If you’re new to the API Explorer, it’s the same tool you’ll use to test and generate code snippets for any API exposed by the Dashboard. --- ## 2️⃣ Find the “Device Connector Versions” API | Action | Where to look | Screenshot hint | |--------|---------------|------------------| | 1 | In the API Explorer, you’ll see a list of available APIs grouped by category. Expand the **Device Management** (or similar) group. | ![API groups](https://example.com/api-groups.png) | | 2 | Locate the entry titled **Get Device Connector Versions** (or the exact name you saw in the docs). Click it to open the detail view. | ![API detail](https://example.com/api-detail.png) | > **Note:** The API you’re after is usually a **GET** operation on a path like `/api/v1/device_connector_versions`. --- ## 3️⃣ Fill in Parameters (if any) | Parameter | Type | Example value | Notes | |-----------|------|---------------|-------| | `device_id` | Path / Query | `12345` | If the API requires a specific device ID, enter it here. | | `format` | Query | `json` | Some APIs let you specify output format; default is often JSON. | > **If the API has no required parameters**, you can skip this step. --- ## 4️⃣ Generate the Request | Step | What to do | Screenshot hint | |------|------------|------------------| | 1 | Once all required fields are populated, click the **Generate Request** button at the bottom of the page. | ![Generate button](https://example.com/generate-button.png) | | 2 | A modal will pop up showing the raw HTTP request. You’ll see the method (`GET`), full URL, headers, and any body (for GET, usually none). | ![Generated request](https://example.com/generated-request.png) | | 3 | Copy the entire block (or just the cURL line) to your clipboard. | ![Copy button](https://example.com/copy-button.png) | --- ## 5️⃣ Authentication – How to Get the Token | Method | How to obtain | Where to put it | |--------|---------------|-----------------| | **Bearer Token** | 1. In the Dashboard, go to **User Settings** → **API Tokens**.
2. Click **Create Token** (you may need admin rights).
3. Copy the generated token. | In the generated request, replace `` with the token you just copied. | | **Basic Auth** | 1. Use your username/password directly in the header: `Authorization: Basic `. | Replace `` with the base64‑encoded string. | > **Security note:** Never expose your token in public scripts or repos. Store it in a secure vault or environment variable. --- ## 6️⃣ Quick‑Copy cURL Example Once you’ve replaced the placeholders, your final cURL might look like this: ```bash curl -X GET \ "https://nexus-dashboard.example.com/api/v1/device_connector_versions" \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " ``` If the API requires a device ID: ```bash curl -X GET \ "https://nexus-dashboard.example.com/api/v1/devices/12345/connector_versions" \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " ``` --- ## 7️⃣ Test It Out | Tool | How to paste | |------|--------------| | **Terminal** | Paste the cURL command and press **Enter**. | | **Postman** | Create a new **GET** request, paste the URL, add the `Authorization` header manually, and hit **Send**. | | **API Explorer** | After generating, you can click **Run** inside the modal to execute it right there. | You should receive a JSON payload listing the connector versions for the requested device(s). --- ## 8️⃣ Save or Export the Generated Code | Option | How to do it | |--------|--------------| | **Save to File** | In the API Explorer modal, click **Export** → **Download JSON** (or **Download cURL**). | | **Copy to Clipboard** | Click the **Copy** icon next to the generated code snippet. | | **Generate SDK** | Some dashboards allow you to generate client libraries (Python, Java, etc.) directly from the API definition. Look for a **Generate SDK** button. | --- ### Recap Checklist 1. **Open API Explorer** → find the API → click it. 2. **Fill required parameters** (if any). 3. **Click Generate Request** → copy the request. 4. **Replace placeholders** (``, ``, etc.). 5. **Execute** via terminal/Postman/API Explorer. That’s it! You now have a fully‑formed RESTful request you can run against your Cisco Nexus Dashboard instance. Happy querying!
